methods.label: Factor toward the nearby power of 2
methods.explanation:
The requested numbers are near \(64=2^6\), suggesting the factors \(2^6-1\) and \(2^6+1\). Repeatedly applying the difference-of-squares identity reveals both:
\[2^{48}-1=(2^{24}-1)(2^{24}+1)\]
\[=(2^{12}-1)(2^{12}+1)(2^{24}+1)\]
\[=(2^6-1)(2^6+1)(2^{12}+1)(2^{24}+1).\]
Thus \(63=2^6-1\) and \(65=2^6+1\) each divide \(2^{48}-1\), because each appears as a factor in an integer product.

Both are between \(60\) and \(70\). The question states that exactly two numbers in this interval divide the given integer, so these two distinct divisors are the required pair: \(\boxed{63,65}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
